submitted.rationale: Index 4 (Bi 0.40, Cu 0.19, V 0.41) gave the highest photocurrent of the three measurements, 8.28e-6 A. This Bi≈V, low-Cu composition is close to BiVO4, a visible-light photoanode.

rejected.reason: Measured 3.17e-6 A. The Cu-vanadate-rich region is weaker.
Measured 9.8e-7 A. Very close in composition to index 4 but gave a much lower photocurrent.

consultations.verdict: Mostly uninformative for this candidate: Cu2O is stable (on hull) but is a Cu-rich reference phase, not relevant to index 4. Choosing index 4 (Bi≈V, lowest Cu) as closest to BiVO4, a known visible-light photoanode (Eg ~2.4 eV < 2.72 eV photons).

Weakly informative: V2O5 HSE gap 2.83 eV is just above the 2.72 eV photon energy, so V-rich binaries absorb poorly; Cu incorporation (copper vanadates, Eg ~2.0 eV) should red-shift absorption. Supports probing the Cu-vanadate region (index 44, Cu 0.52 / V 0.39) as a contrast to the BiVO4-like region.

Against Cu-rich compositions: Cu2O (1.56 eV) is a small-gap p-type phase; Cu-rich phases give photocathodic or poor anodic behaviour, which matches the low value at index 44. This supports keeping Cu minimal. Index 7 (lowest Cu, 0.18, Bi≈V) is closest to BiVO4, which fits with index 4 (8.3 µA) being the best result so far.
